ABSTRACT: To understand the efects of additives on the performance of a Ni−
Co−P alloy electroplated coating, this study, based on a single-factor experiment,
utilized a Box−Behnken experimental design to optimize an additive that can
enhance the electrodeposited Ni−Co−P alloy coating’s properties, including
hardness, glossiness, and corrosion resistance. The study used tools such as a
gloss meter, a Vickers hardness tester, and an electrochemical workstation to analyze
the impact of diferent additives on the coating’s hardness and gloss. The optimal
additive combination was determined. The results from the Box−Behnken
experiment showed that when the concentrations of sodium dodecyl sulfate,
thiourea, and sodium allyl sulfonate reached 0.10, 0.15, and 0.22 g/L, respectively,
the resulting coating hardness was 475.4
\mathrm { H V } _ { 0 . 5 } ,
and the gloss level was 463.4 GU.
Compared to the coatings without additives, the hardness increased by 90.34
\mathrm { H V } _ { 0 . 5 } ,
and the glossiness rose by 101.2 GU. The coating’s corrosion resistance also

of brighteners such as thiourea or
-butyne diol reduces or

additives hinder the discharge of metal ions, increasing the
overpotential for the reaction and promoting nucleation. This
results in finer grain size and denser coatings, leading to
increased hardness and glossiness.<sup>14</sup> However, at higher

metal ions are greatly afected or complexed by a large number
of brightener molecules during the discharge process, severely
hindering the normal deposition process. This intensifies the
hydrogen evolution reaction and leads to a decrease in coating
hardness and glossiness.<sup>20−22</sup>
In accordance with the
comparative analysis, thiourea, which showed a greater
improvement in coating hardness and glossiness, served as
the brightener for the plating solution system.
